subject: Token attribution misalignment after large ingestion job
messages:
From: Anna Lowe <anna@finnapps.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: billing@finnapps.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected token increase after ingestion job

Hi Vivek,

We noticed a sharp increase in token consumption that appears to coincide with a large embeddings ingestion job FinnApps ran on 2027-04-10. A summary from our side:
- 2027-04-10 03:00-06:00 PDT: ~2.1M tokens billed
- Typical day: ~120k tokens
- Roughly 85% of the spike shows up under project "finnapps-archive" which we did not expect (we expected the job to map to "finnapps-ingest").

I've attached the ingestion manifest and a short CSV that maps our batch IDs to your request_ids (finnapps_ingest_manifest_20270410.csv). Can you help explain why attribution landed on the other project and whether these tokens were generated during streaming calls vs batch uploads?

We have an outstanding invoice (INV-4591) scheduled next week and we'd like to put a short hold on collection if this is something that will be adjusted. Also — please advise whether VAT will apply to any adjustments.

Thanks for the quick look,
Anna Lowe
Head of Data Platform
FinnApps

Attachments: finnapps_ingest_manifest_20270410.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lowe <anna@finnapps.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, billing@finnapps.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token increase after ingestion job

Thanks Anna — and sorry for the surprise. I’ve looped in Rachel from Billing so we can assess whether a credit is appropriate and how VAT would flow.

Quick asks to triage faster:
1) Can you confirm the exact request_ids in the attached manifest that map to the times you cited (03:00-06:00 PDT)?
2) Can you share a small sample of the usage export for those hostnames/request_ids (a 1k-line JSONL or CSV is perfect).
3) Did the ingestion job rotate keys or use multiple API keys during the run?

On our side I’ve attached a short guide to pull a pre-filtered usage export if easier (redwood_usage_export_instructions.txt). If you prefer, we can pull the export once we have the job IDs.

I’ll start a preliminary look at sessions and attribution. If there’s a clear misattribution we’ll hold collection while we reconcile.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_usage_export_instructions.txt

From: Anna Lowe <anna@finnapps.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: billing@finnapps.com, trevor@finnapps.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token increase after ingestion job

Hi Vivek — thanks. Attached is a 1k-line sample of the usage export we pulled for the 03:00-06:00 window (usage_sample_20270410-13.jsonl). Request IDs and batch IDs are in there. We did not rotate API keys during the job — same key for the whole run.

Important to note: our procurement team is asking whether this will be considered a customer-caused billing event (in which case they will pay) vs something you will credit. They have also requested confirmation on VAT treatment if a credit is issued — is VAT reversed on the credit or applied differently?

Please advise on next steps. We’d prefer to keep INV-4591 on hold until you confirm.

Regards,
Anna

Attachments: usage_sample_20270410-13.jsonl

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected token increase after ingestion job — internal analysis request

Team — forwarding FinnApps thread and attached usage sample. Quick notes from my triage:
- I instrumented an initial query against the usage logs and saw ~1.8M tokens attributed to ~48k short-lived sessions created during the ingest window. Session keys appear to have been reused by the SDK in a manner that caused tokens to be attributed to the wrong project in our aggregation layer.
- hypothesis: when multiple ephemeral sessions are opened and the SDK rotates session tokens mid-job, our attribution fallback can pick the nearest active project tag. This looks like a server-side attribution bug (edge case for large parallel batch imports).

Proposed plan:
1) Product (Priyom) to confirm root cause and scope of clients potentially affected in last 90 days.
2) Billing (Rachel) to compute a provisional credit for the misattributed tokens and advise on VAT handling (reverse-charge vs credit note).
3) CS (me) to propose credit to FinnApps and keep invoice on hold until resolved.

Attachments: ingest_session_trace.log (extracted traces showing session reuse).

Priyom — any quick thoughts? If you confirm a server-side bug I think we should proactively credit the misattributed portion and schedule a fix next sprint.

— Vivek

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lowe <anna@finnapps.com>, billing@finnapps.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected token increase after ingestion job

Hi Anna / FinnApps team — and thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and resolution: 

What we found
- Root cause: our attribution service misattributed ~1.45M tokens (of the ~2.1M spike) to a fallback project when many ephemeral sessions were created during parallel batch ingestion. Product has confirmed this is a server-side attribution bug that can surface for large, parallel imports.
- Affected window: 2027-04-10 03:05–05:57 PDT

What we are doing
- Billing: Rachel will apply a provisional credit of USD 9,200 to offset the misattributed tokens; this will appear on your next invoice as a line-item "Provisional credit — attribution correction".
- VAT: Credits reduce the net taxable amount. Rachel will issue a credit note that references INV-4591; our finance team will apply VAT reversal per the normal credit-note process for US/EU taxes — we will send the credit note and VAT details when the credit posts.
- Product: We’ve scheduled a code fix to harden attribution when ephemeral sessions are used; patch targeted for 2027-04-29 release.

Attachments & evidence
- I’ve attached our extracted session trace that shows session-id reuse for the ingestion job (ingest_session_trace.log). We are also providing a filtered usage export for the affected window; link above.

Next steps / asks for you
1) Please confirm that applying the provisional credit and releasing INV-4591 from hold is acceptable to FinnApps.
2) If you need a different credit amount or want us to escalate to finance for a manual invoice adjustment now, tell us and we’ll route immediately.

If you confirm, Rachel will post the credit note and I’ll mark the ticket (HUBSPOT-1234567) resolved. Sorry again for the disruption — we’ll follow up after the attribution hardening lands.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ingest_session_trace.log
